prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. Injury: whiplash. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1402; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, but my counsel can confirm the details for the transcript.

Q: Fair enough. Let's talk about the accident. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in League City, Texas, in the right lane.

Q: What happened next?
A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. My car was pushed forward into the intersection, and my head snapped back and then forward against the headrest.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not really. I saw headlights in my mirror a second before it hit, but I didn't have time to react.

Q: Did you get out of the car at the scene?
A: Yes, I stood up on the shoulder for a few minutes. My neck already felt stiff, and I had a dull ache across my shoulders.

Q: Did you go to a doctor or seek medical care after the accident?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same evening. They checked my range of motion, gave me a prescription for a muscle relaxant, and told me I had whiplash.

Q: Have you received any other treatment since then?
A: Yes, I started physical therapy about two weeks later, going two or three times a week. I also see my primary care doctor when the pain flares up.

Q: How would you describe your pain now compared to right after the accident?
A: It's changed. In the beginning, the pain was sharp and constant. Now it's more of a deep ache that comes and goes, and it gets worse when I sit at a desk for long periods or turn my head quickly to check traffic.

Q: How has this affected your daily life?
A: I used to coach my nephew's soccer team on weekends, and I've had to step back from that. Lifting groceries is harder, and I sleep poorly because I can't find a comfortable position. I also avoid driving at night because turning to look over my shoulder hurts.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: I missed about a week when the pain was at its worst. Since then I've been working at my desk with a lumbar support cushion and taking breaks to stretch.

Q: Before this accident, did you have any problems with your neck or back?
A: I had some occasional stiffness after long days at work, but nothing that stopped me from doing my normal activities or required a doctor's visit.

Q: Thank you. I have no further questions at this time.
A: Thank you.
